transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Lee. Um, well, what brings me in is that I just keep getting hit out of nowhere with... with the scene of my cousin on that pavement. It's like I can actually hear the shouting and see the lights all over again. And it happens even when I'm just standing in the church office, you know, trying to act normal.
How long ago did your cousin's accident happen?
It's been... well, this has been going on since he was killed. That was two years and three months ago.
Since the accident, have you found yourself avoiding certain places, conversations, or activities that remind you of what happened to your cousin?

Yeah, I do. Um, I actually take the long way around town now, just so I don't have to pass the community center or that court. And... if somebody brings it up and starts talking about that night, I just shut it down. Or I'll find some reason to excuse myself and leave. I just can't do it.
Since your cousin's death, have you noticed yourself feeling unusually jumpy or on edge, like you startle easily or feel like you always need to be on alert for danger?

Yeah, definitely. I mean... I can't even sit with my back to a door anymore. And when I'm at church events, I'm supposed to be engaging with folks, but I'm just... I'm always watching people's hands, or checking the corners of the room. If a car slows down outside, I'm staring at it. I spend the whole time figuring out where the nearest exit is instead of actually paying attention to the people standing right in front of me.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient developed intrusive re-experiencing (flashbacks with sensory detail), persistent avoidance of trauma-related reminders, and hyperarousal/hypervigilance symptoms following the sudden violent death of her cousin. Symptoms have persisted for over two years, are directly linked to a clearly identifiable traumatic event, and are causing functional impairment in social/occupational contexts (church work). This symptom cluster and duration are consistent with Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (F43.1) rather than an acute stress reaction (which resolves within a month) or generalized anxiety disorder (which lacks a specific traumatic trigger and re-experiencing symptoms).

confirmed_symptoms: Involuntary vivid flashbacks of the traumatic scene (seeing lights, hearing shouting)
Intrusive memories occurring in unrelated settings (e.g., at church office)
Avoids specific locations associated with the trauma (community center, court)
Avoids conversations or reminders about the event, shutting down discussion or leaving
Hypervigilance (watching hands, scanning corners, monitoring exits)
Exaggerated startle response to environmental cues (e.g., cars slowing down)
Inability to sit with back to door, indicating heightened alertness

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Symptoms have persisted continuously for over 2 years and 3 months since the traumatic event (cousin's death), exceeding the 1-month threshold required to distinguish PTSD from acute stress reaction.
additional_requirements: Clear temporal link between traumatic event (cousin's violent death) and symptom onset
Symptoms cause impairment in social/occupational functioning (church duties)
Symptom cluster includes all three core PTSD domains: intrusion, avoidance, and hyperarousal
